transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC, Duration 42m
Attendees: Marco Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Evan Park (Aurora CTO), Sara Gomez (Aurora ML Eng), Ryan Holt (Aurora Platform)

--- Summary / Topics (auto) ---
Summary: demo of JSON mode + schemas, tool/function calling, Console & Optimize suggestions, security Qs
Topics: structured output, function calling, guardrails, deployment options, pilot next steps

00:00:03 Marco: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we'll keep this to about 40 minutes, quick intros, and then Priya will jump into the structured output demo
00:00:10 Evan: sounds good, Evan Park here, CTO at Aurora, Sara and Ryan on the call too
00:00:15 Sara: hi all
00:00:18 Ryan: hey
00:00:25 Priya: awesome, so i'll share my screen, this session is gonna show JSON-mode (our structured output), a couple of schemas, and then a live function-calling/demo with a mock TMS tool. please forgive any audio artifacts, my connection is fine but fireflies might mangle a few words
00:00:45 Marco: quick note on goals — you mentioned wanting deterministic outputs for downstream pipelines, right evan?
00:00:52 Evan: yeah exactly, we can't have engineers doing massive parsing fixes, need stable schema + validation and clear error/fallbacks
00:01:05 Priya: perfect. ok starting the demo. first slide, JSON-mode: you can define a JSON schema in the Console or via API, redwood will return structured JSON and enforce shape, we also have configurable guardrails to coerce or reject outputs that don't match
00:01:36 Sara: when you say enforce, do you mean runtime validation or pre-output prompting? like which layer ensures shape?
00:01:46 Priya: good q, it's multi-layer: prompt-level schema guidance + model-level sampling parameters + an automatic post-output validator. the Console shows realtime validation results and optional auto-rewrite attempts to coerce into schema. if coercion fails, you can trigger a fallback policy (e.g. call a simpler model or return an error with confidence score)
00:02:12 Ryan: is there a limit on schema size? our shipments have nested arrays and up to 30 keys per object
00:02:22 Priya: schemas up to a few KB are fine, deeply nested is supported but we recommend flattening arrays where possible for latency. if you need, we can demo with your sample payloads in the pilot
00:02:40 Marco: demoing live: sending a prompt to the API in JSON mode, schema defined for shipment-update with fields: shipment_id, status, eta, location {lat,lng}, events[] where events have type,timestamp,actor
00:03:05 Priya: starting a live call... streaming on, you can see the response stream; note the tokens are emitted as structured JSON tokens so your parser can start consuming earlier
00:03:30 (transcription glitch) Speaker 6: ...k-v cash...
00:03:35 Priya: ha that's fireflies, i said KV cache, not K-V cash, sorry
00:03:45 Sara: that's ok
00:03:50 Priya: response comes back and it matches the schema, we show validation: pass, confidence 0.89. if it had extra keys we can strip or move to metadata
00:04:20 Evan: what about hallucinations — say the model invents an ETA? how do you handle that?
00:04:30 Priya: two things: schema can mark fields as required and/or trusted sources; second, we support function-calling where the model can emit a structured intent and the platform will call your canonical service (e.g., our tool connector calls your TMS POST /update) instead of letting model invent values
00:04:55 Marco: and the tool-calling flow can be recorded in audit logs, with request/response payloads, timestamps, and user tokens for later review
00:05:12 Ryan: audit logs retention — is that configurable, and can they be routed to our S3 or Splunk?
00:05:20 Priya: yes configurable retention in Console, and you can set up sink connectors to S3, GCS, or stream to your SIEM. KMS integration for encrypting logs at rest is supported
00:05:40 Sara: demo the function-calling? would love to see the error path too
00:05:46 Priya: sure. i'm calling a mock 'upsertShipment' tool. model returns a function call with args that strictly conform to the tool schema, we then invoke your endpoint. watch the UI show the call, response, and automatic retry policy (we have 429/backoff and circuit-breaker settings)
00:06:20 (15s gap of screen transition)
00:06:35 Priya: ok the tool returned 200 but with a validation diff — the endpoint accepted 'eta' as string, schema expected ISO8601; Console highlights mismatch and suggests an auto-normalize rule, we can either push the normalized value back or log as discrepancy
00:07:00 Evan: good, that's the sort of thing we need to triage; can the Console export the validation diffs as a CSV?
00:07:10 Priya: yes exportable, and Optimize will surface frequent diffs as regression alerts so you can add a schema tweak or model prompt patch
00:07:30 Marco: switching to Optimize: here's where we suggest batching and quantization profiles per workload. for high-throughput shipment enrichment we suggested dynamic batching with a target latency 120 ms p95 and a 4-bit quantization profile on A100 to cut costs by ~40% in our bench
00:07:58 Ryan: curious — how safe is 4-bit quant for factual fields vs free-text descriptions?
00:08:06 Priya: factual structured fields are usually stable under quant; we recommend mixed strategy: keep decoder/head in higher precision for names/IDs and quantize heavier matrices. Optimize provides model-specific recommendations and a simulated cost/latency tradeoff chart in the Console
00:08:30 Sara: can we run a quick smoke benchmark during the pilot? we want to hit 1000 updates/min with <200ms median
00:08:40 Marco: yes, pilot checklist will include a small load test; we'll run both hosted and Dedicated routing to compare throughput and tail latency
00:09:00 Evan: Dedicated — quick Q: we need private network access, our compliance team wants VPC peering and customer-managed KMS. how does Redwood Private address that?
00:09:15 Priya: Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem control plane options, you can bring your own KMS/HSM, direct peering or transit VPC, plus audit logs stored inside your account. we have an enterprise package for that with SOC2 Type II and ISO docs attached
00:09:38 Ryan: do you support SAML SSO + SCIM?
00:09:42 Marco: yep, SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, RBAC fine-grained roles — we'll share our security pack after the call
00:09:55 (small cross talk)
00:10:05 Priya: back to the demo, showing guardrails: you can set hard rejects for certain fields (e.g., PII), or soft masks. I'm toggling a guardrail to reject any output with personal_phone or ssn keys — watch the validation reject and route to fallback
00:10:30 Sara: do you have automated PII detectors or do we bring our own?
00:10:35 Priya: both. we have built-in detectors, and you can plug in your own classifier via function-call hook; detection events are surfaced in Console with redaction suggestions
00:10:55 Marco: pricing note — structured-output with schema enforcement is within standard token pricing, tool-calling adds a small per-call transaction fee for logging and connectors; Dedicated pricing is separate as usual
00:11:18 Evan: can you show the API payload for JSON-mode? we'd like to see curl example for our infra folks
00:11:24 Priya: sure. in the Console there's a code snippet; sending content-type application/json, top-level 'schema' param or schema_id, 'mode': 'json', and 'tool_calls': true. i'll paste a sample into the chat after
00:11:45 (fireflies note: shared link to sample repo pasted)
00:11:50 Marco: we'll also share a small node/python client snippet to validate responses locally before ingestion
00:12:05 Sara: question on retries — if the model suggests an update and the endpoint returns 5xx, does Redwood retry automatically?
00:12:12 Priya: yes configurable retries and backoff; you can set total retry budget and whether to surface failed attempts in the calling thread
00:12:28 Evan: how are errors surfaced to our downstream? we want predictable error codes so our orchestrator can route to manual review queues
00:12:36 Priya: we return structured error objects with reason codes: validation_failed, tool_error, model_low_confidence, rate_limit. you can map these in your pipeline
00:12:50 (short pause)
00:13:10 Marco: let's pivot to the pilot plan — 1-week pilot: two endpoints, 1) hosted sandbox with sample payloads and 2) your VPC Dedicated environment for a live run. objectives: validate schema stability, measure latency/cost, check guardrail false positives
00:13:35 Evan: timeline: we can allocate infra for the week of 3/23, security sign-off dependent on quick review of SOC2 pack
00:13:48 Marco: ok we'll send security pack and a short pilot playbook. Priya, can you outline bench configs?
00:13:55 Priya: yes. bench plan: 1) 100/min smoke, 2) ramp to 1k/min for 10 minutes, 3) tail-latency check at p95/p99, and 4) two model variants: base open model and a quantized variant; we'll collect token counts and cost estimates
00:14:20 Ryan: can you provide the exact IAM/network steps for VPC peering? our network team wants a checklist
00:14:28 Marco: yes we'll include a step-by-step; also a template terraform for peering and routing rules
00:14:40 Evan: any concerns about regulated data? we handle PII for customs forms in some regions
00:14:48 Priya: with Private deployment and customer-managed KMS, data-at-rest and in-transit encryption meet typical compliance needs; we can also arrange for an NDA and a short security call with our compliance lead
00:15:10 (noise)
00:15:30 Marco: quick objection — what if we hit a model regression after deploy? how do you detect and rollback?
00:15:36 Priya: Optimize has quality monitors tied to your eval sets and production prompts. it will raise regression alerts and can trigger an automatic model fallback to a previous pinned version while you investigate
00:15:55 Sara: how does that interact with cached KV states for long-running chats?
00:16:05 Priya: KV cache is per model variant and we can invalidate caches on rollout. there's also a migration helper to warm new cache states from sampled traffic to avoid cold-start regressions
00:16:22 Evan: this sounds useful. ok, final Q: can we get a cost estimate for 1M tokens/month with the suggested config?
00:16:31 Marco: we'll include a cost worksheet in the follow-up; Optimize will also simulate cost under different batching/quantization assumptions
00:16:45 (brief silence)
00:17:00 Priya: wrapping up, i'll drop the sample repo, API snippets, and a pilot playbook in the chat. any last minute questions?
00:17:10 Ryan: none here
00:17:12 Sara: just please include the validation diffs export example
00:17:20 Evan: thanks, this was helpful. we'll sync internally and aim to send sample payloads and SSO contact info by next week
00:17:30 Marco: great. recap of next steps: share security pack & demo recording, agree pilot week, sample payloads from Aurora. action items recorded. thanks everyone
00:17:45 (call ends)
